rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The diff push-back ('Read the diff and push back on a line') is a real forcing function carried entirely in body prose with no fenced prompt — deliberately: 'No pre-made prompt for the pushback... your push-back is what becomes a rule.' A prompt would defeat the move (the wording has to be the student's own, reused verbatim at the compound step). Backing block's Stance section names this as the exercise's one genuinely contested claim, so the absence of a fence is the design, not an omission. The other three forcing functions (write-test-and-fix, interrogate, optional second TDD pass) are correctly fenced (fix-tests-first-1/2/3).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Self-study (no trainer to narrate the slide live) carries a real risk this beat gets skipped by a student who only pastes fences — already logged in the sim trace's confusion_flags as an accepted, unresolved-by-design gap; no action needed unless the self-study delivery mode changes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room. Body does NOT author conversations.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'discuss with', 'share with your neighbor', 'tell the room' or pair/group cue anywhere in the body. Every sentence is about the work (the test, the diff, the fix, the PR) or the student's own solo judgment call, never cohort pacing or comparison.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named; mood-floor 8+/10 on teaching beats.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Sim trace: this is a TEACHING beat (not setup) — phase mood_score 8, close mood_score 8, both at the ship bar. module_mood_contract = M1 joyful creation. The tightened lead-in trio ('a failing test... the smallest fix... a shipped PR' / 'pushing back is core work') keeps the artifact contract legible without previewing the diff.

The reframed push-back line — 'The agent yields if you push hard enough, so its agreement settles nothing. Whether your argument was actually better is your call' — and 'There is always a next plausible answer... when to stop digging is your call' both frame the student's uncertainty as not-knowing-yet, never as having-done-wrong. No shame-register language anywhere in the file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'The point: pushing back is core work.' and 'Tests-first, root-cause-driven.' are both positive-discipline titles, not failure words ('fabrication', 'rubber-stamping', etc. appear only in the maintainer/trainer-facing block, never as a student-facing lead).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check (consolidates front-run check, module-to-module arc, Big Idea fidelity, mood doesn't resolve early).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Front-run: 'No plan mode here. On a trivial bug, plan mode is overhead' matches the strategy doc's M1-in-detail note verbatim in spirit ('No plan mode in M1... M2 is the subject') and does not front-run M2's plan-mode-at-depth teaching moment. Module-to-module arc: 'Hand off to the ticket close' matches the strategy doc's 'Stop there; the ticket and the compound step come after' — no front-run of close-the-ticket or compound-and-close. Big Idea fidelity: 'pushing back is core work' is the exercise's own Antti-directed point (commit bc8e9e6, same-day, part of the M1 three-point set: 'the context window is not your codebase' / 'pushing back is core work' / 'every push-back is a hint toward your own rules') — read together as an arc per check_strategy_tie_in.md §6d's spirit. Mood doesn't resolve early: the file stays inside M1's joyful-creation register throughout; it doesn't reach for M2's grounded-competence or M3's earned-trust framing.
